title: Delete the dead TrackOrder aggregate/OrderingLevel enum or fix its doc comment's false repository contract
why: TrackOrder and OrderingLevel have zero references anywhere else in lib/ (grep confirms) — the actual TrackLearningOrderRepository interface returns bare List<LearningOrderItem> from getSedarimOrder/getMasechtosOrder, never a TrackOrder. But track_order.dart's own doc comment asserts '[TrackLearningOrderRepository] returns a [TrackOrder] from getSedarimOrder / getMasechtosOrder' — a confident, specific, and false description of the current contract. A future maintainer (e.g. picking up the W4.22 refactor referenced in masechta_ordering_policy.dart) who trusts this comment will build against an aggregate the real code never produces. Separately, TrackOrder hand-writes ==/hashCode/toString instead of using @freezed like every other domain model in this batch (StageDefinition, GoalEntity), and its hashCode only hashes items.length, so any two same-length differently-ordered TrackOrders collide.
recommendation: Delete the file if the two-method-pair API is staying; if TrackOrder is genuinely planned to replace it, land that refactor (repository returns TrackOrder, callers updated) in the same change as the doc comment, and convert it to @freezed while doing so.
acceptance_criteria: Either track_order.dart is removed, or TrackLearningOrderRepository's methods actually return TrackOrder and the doc comment is true.
If kept, TrackOrder is a @freezed class with generated ==/hashCode, not hand-written ones.
`flutter analyze` and existing track_order tests stay green.

corrections: docs/planning/tech-debt-remediation-plan.md lines 88 ('W4.12-W4.15 ... TrackOrder'), 404 ('□ W4.15 ... TrackOrder aggregate, OrderingLevel'), 413 ('□ W4.22 ... MasechtaOrderingPolicy (already W4.15)') show this is a tracked, partially-executed refactor step, not abandoned dead code as the title implies. The finding's own hedged alternative ('if genuinely planned, land the refactor') is actually the correct branch — the primary 'Delete the dead...' framing/title is misleading given this evidence, even though the false present-tense doc comment and non-@freezed hand-rolled equality are independently real and worth fixing.
